function.mechanism: Dissociates into magnesium and chloride ions that increase ionic strength; magnesium ions support coagulation/firming effects in some food systems.
common_food_categories: tofu/soy product coagulation systems (bittern-derived use context)

adi.basis: EFSA (2019) did not set a numerical ADI in the abstract; it identified 40 mg chloride/kg bw/day as a reference value for safety assessment.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA concluded that exposure to chloride from E507/E508/E509/E511 does not raise a safety concern at reported use levels, although high-percentile exposure in some children exceeded the chloride reference value.

adi.basis: JECFA chemical entry states ADI NOT LIMITED; included in ADI group for hydrochloric acid and bases.

concerns.summary: Very high oral intake can cause severe hypermagnesemia; fatal and non-fatal human case reports exist for magnesium chloride/bittern ingestion.
In intoxication context, hypermagnesemia has been associated with ECG changes (e.g., QT prolongation) and can progress to serious cardiopulmonary effects if untreated.
Animal data show dose-related oral toxicity at high dietary concentrations (kidney tubular vacuolation and reduced body weight in mice at >=2.5% dietary magnesium chloride).

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA reported no concern for genotoxicity and carcinogenicity in the chloride additive group assessment.
Long-term mouse feeding study reported lack of carcinogenicity for magnesium chloride hexahydrate.
EFSA concluded no safety concern for chloride exposure from E507/E508/E509/E511 at reported use levels.
FDA lists magnesium chloride as GRAS under 21 CFR 184.1426.
JECFA lists ADI as NOT LIMITED.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA high-percentile chloride exposure estimates for E507/E508/E509/E511 were slightly above the 40 mg chloride/kg bw/day reference value in some younger age groups, while mean estimates were at or below the reference value.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory evaluations converge on low concern at authorized use levels (EFSA no safety concern; FDA GRAS; JECFA ADI not limited). Evidence against risk_free comes from high-dose animal toxicity, severe intoxication case reports, and high-percentile chloride exposure above EFSA's reference value in some children.
key_factors: EFSA 2019 conclusion of no safety concern at reported use levels
FDA GRAS status and CGMP-based use conditions in 21 CFR 184.1426
JECFA ADI NOT LIMITED (group ADI context)
No IARC listing for magnesium chloride in the current classifications dataset
Human poisoning cases show toxicity at excessive intake
EFSA high-percentile chloride exposure exceedance in some child groups
